explanation: Template class specialization in C++ allows developers to define custom implementations of a class template for specific types or conditions. This feature enables optimized or tailored behavior when the generic template does not suffice, enhancing flexibility and efficiency in generic programming. It is particularly useful in the context of the Standard Template Library (STL) and modern C++ idioms, where generic containers and algorithms benefit from specialized behavior for certain data types.
code_example: // General template for a container wrapper
c2.display(); // Outputs: Specialized container for int
example_explanation: This example demonstrates template class specialization by defining a general template class 'Container' for any type T, and providing a full specialization for the 'int' type. When creating instances of 'Container<double>', the generic implementation is used, displaying 'Generic container'. For 'Container<int>', the specialized implementation is invoked, displaying 'Specialized container for int'. This showcases how specialization allows customizing class behavior for specific data types within C++'s template system, a core feature for writing flexible and efficient generic code.
